# EvEmptyState

> An empty state fills a screen or container when there's no content to show — errors (400 / 401 / 404 / 500), maintenance, or simply no data / no results. It pairs an illustration with a message and an optional recovery action.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:empty-state` |
| Layer | Organism (`src/organisms`) |
| Import | `import { EvEmptyState } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvEmptyState>` or `<ev-empty-state>` |
| Source | `src/organisms/empty-state/EvEmptyState.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-empty-state">` |


## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Empty**, frame `4272:79658` (Empty State). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Whenever a view has nothing to render — failed requests, missing permissions, not-found pages, server errors, maintenance windows, or empty lists / search results.

### When not to use

- For transient loading → use a skeleton or spinner. For a single empty field → use an inline Hint, not a full-screen error state.

### Do

- Match the state to the cause (status code or empty-data). Keep the message human and brief. Offer a clear next step (Reload, Go Back). Use the smaller No Data / No Result variants inside tables and cards.

### Don't

- Don't show a blank screen with no guidance. Don't blame the user. Don't use a page-level error for an in-table empty result.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvEmptyState`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-empty-state">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:empty-state` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
